facts.raw_span: 2-year history of progressively worsening fever
weight loss, night sweats, and a dry cough
chronic lower back pain without neurologic deficits
painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux
two sputum GeneXpert tests at local clinics, both negative
Hemoglobin 10.9 g/dL
ESR >130 mm/hr
CRP 113 mg/L
induced sputum was trace positive for MTB on GeneXpert
biopsy of the toe ulcer showed necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with a solitary acid-fast bacillus
Chest radiograph showed bilateral reticular-nodular opacities
MRI of the spine revealed contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection causing spinal cord compression

concepts.why: The patient's symptoms and laboratory results, including a trace positive GeneXpert test, necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacillus on biopsy, and contiguous spondylitis on MRI, are consistent with tuberculosis.

The patient's chronic lower back pain and MRI findings of contiguous spondylitis from T6 to T10 with discitis and an epidural/paraspinal collection are consistent with Pott's disease, a form of tuberculosis that affects the spine.

The patient's bilateral reticular-nodular opacities on chest radiograph and trace positive GeneXpert test are consistent with miliary tuberculosis, a form of tuberculosis characterized by widespread dissemination of the bacteria.
The patient's painful nonhealing ulcer on his right hallux and biopsy findings of necrotizing granulomatous inflammation with acid-fast bacillus are consistent with cutaneous tuberculosis.
The patient's elevated ESR and CRP, and urine findings of granular casts and leukocytes, are consistent with renal tuberculosis, although the diagnosis would require further confirmation.
